current_paper2_main_finding_candidate.narrative: Atomic MLIP energy descriptor (W_eq) does NOT correlate with experimental SE/NCM adhesion (R=-0.76, anti-correlated). However, GEOMETRIC bond density at equilibrium gap reproduces experimental ranking: Li-O attractive (R=+0.82) and Cl-O anti-correlated (R=-0.91). Composite (Li-O − α·Cl-O) gives R=+0.91. Vacancy chemical anchor mechanism manifests geometrically: Li5.4 vacancy positions surface Li closer to NCM-O while suppressing Cl exposure.

relax_vs_rigid_bond_count_argument.user_question: if descriptor is geometric bond count, is relaxation more realistic?
relax_vs_rigid_bond_count_argument.type_a_local_relaxation: Atoms adjust 0.1-0.5 Å to find optimal bonding positions — this is what we WANT
relax_vs_rigid_bond_count_argument.type_b_long_range_migration: Li atoms migrate 3+ Å into NCM bulk = solid solution formation = NOT adhesion. v9-v11 LBFGS (200-300 steps) gave type-b artifact.
relax_vs_rigid_bond_count_argument.v22_strategy: Limited LBFGS (max 50 steps, fmax 0.05) + FixAtoms NCM bot 1/3 + SE top 1/3 → cap migration, allow only type-a. Track RMS displacement; if >1.5 Å, flag as migration.
relax_vs_rigid_bond_count_argument.fallback: If v22 gives same ranking as v15 (rigid), descriptor robust. If different, discuss in paper #2 method choice.
relax_vs_rigid_bond_count_argument.publication_note: Rigid bond density at equilibrium gap is defensible as 'geometric snapshot at favorable separation' — different from but complementary to relaxed bond formation.
